items.title: Large language models' complicit responses to illicit instructions across socio-legal contexts
items.abstract: Large language models may facilitate unlawful activities, yet this risk remains underexplored in studies assessing illicit-content recognition or narrow categories of illicit scenarios. We define complicit facilitation as model guidance that assists users with illicit instructions. To assess it, we develop a legally-informed, automated pipeline grounded in real-world cases and legal frameworks, and introduce EVIL, a benchmark covering 269 illicit scenarios and 50 illicit intents across Chinese and United States legal contexts. Evaluations indicate that complicit facilitation is widespread across models, with legal warnings and lawful alternatives often omitted. Risks vary across socio-legal contexts and are elevated for crimes against societal interests, non-violent offenses, and intents involving subjective motives or deceptive justifications. Models provide more complicit assistance when instructions describe users as older adults, racial minorities, non-religious individuals, or workers in lower-prestige occupations. Existing open-source safety benchmarks and alignment datasets offer limited coverage and mitigation of these risks.

items.title: Lipid Nanoparticles in Drug and Gene Delivery: Current Advances and Future Perspectives
items.abstract: As a cutting-edge non-viral delivery system, lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) are revolutionizing the treatment of drugs and nucleic acids. LNPs are now recognized as adaptable, clinically validated nanocarriers due to their clinical success, as evidenced by approved siRNA therapies and extensively used mRNA vaccines. In order to facilitate effective intracellular cargo release, modern LNPs employ ionizable lipids, which are neutral under physiological conditions but become positively charged in acidic endosomes. Stability, encapsulation efficiency, biodistribution, and therapeutic efficacy have all been enhanced by developments in lipid chemistry, microfluidic manufacturing, surface engineering, and artificial intelligence-assisted formulation. However, obstacles to wider use still include low tissue specificity, ineffective endosomal escape, immunogenicity, production difficulties, and long-term safety. The evolution, composition, formulation, delivery methods, therapeutic uses, clinical translation, regulatory issues, and upcoming tactics like organ-selective targeting and CRISPR-Cas gene editing are all covered in this review.

items.title: Liquid biopsy and cancer therapy: current technology, diagnosis, prognosis, and cancer treatments
items.abstract: Liquid biopsy offers repeated, minimally invasive molecular profiling of cancer, but its clinical value depends on the analyte, analytical platform, and intended use. In this Review, we evaluate current liquid-biopsy technologies for diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment guidance, with a particular emphasize on tumor-derived extracellular vesicles (TDEVs) as a bridge between biomarker detection and therapeutic intervention. We examine genomic and epigenomic profiling, single-cell and single-vesicle analysis, and multi-omics integration as complementary approaches for assessing tumour burden, heterogeneity and treatment response. Circulating tumor DNA genotyping guides targeted therapy in selected advanced cancers, whereas many early-detection and vesicle-based applications require prospective validation. We highlight how the TDEV lipid bilayer protects diverse molecular cargo that reflects evolving tumour phenotypes and how TDEV-mediated communication contributes to metastasis, immune evasion and therapeutic resistance, creating opportunities to target pathogenic vesicle signalling. We also assess engineered vesicles from malignant and non-malignant cells as drug-delivery and cancer-vaccination platforms, while noting that tumour-derived carriers may retain oncogenic or immunosuppressive cargo. Most candidate vesicle biomarkers remain supported by retrospective studies, and therapeutic platforms are largely preclinical or in early clinical testing. We discuss the requirements for clinical translation, including reliable identification of tumour-derived vesicles, standardized workflows and prospective multicentre validation for diagnostics, and reproducible manufacturing, cargo characterization, potency testing and product-specific pharmacokinetic and safety evaluation for therapeutics. Finally, we consider how multimodal profiling and artificial intelligence might improve signal integration, and argue that clinical adoption will depend on demonstrating that vesicle-guided decisions and interventions improve patient outcomes.

items.title: LIS Forward at UMD: Defining the epistemological core of LIS
items.abstract: The field of Library and Information Science (LIS) has faced identity challenges during periods of rapid technological innovation that alter established practices (Chu, 2010; Marcum, 2005). The rise of artificial intelligence, increasing emphasis on data and technology, and discussions of iSchool mergers raise fundamental questions about disciplinary identity, values, and relevance (Gioia & Thomas, 1996; Marques et al., 2024). As an interdisciplinary field, LIS has struggled to define itself within a single conceptual framework and has navigated the tensions between professional education and research (Audunson et al., 2007). These developments compel LIS educators and researchers to redefine knowledge production, management, and dissemination within the field.Building on prior work (Gibson et al., 2025; LIS Forward, 2023; 2025), this study examines how LIS epistemological core is represented and communicated as foundational knowledge in 40 LIS core course syllabi from 10 selected iSchools in the United States. Informed by Erduran and Kaya's (2019) definition of the “epistemic core,” this study employs collaborative thematic analysis to examine course titles, descriptions, learning objectives, and required materials. Based on the analysis, syllabi were coded into four categories: general research, special topics, professional skills development, and research methods. AI use disclaimers and guidance were also examined for any potential patterns across the syllabi. Core courses in MLIS (and related degrees) introduce emerging scholars and practitioners to what is considered foundational to the LIS field, potentially shaping their understanding of LIS epistemological core. The study findings contribute to ongoing efforts to clarify LIS identity, help shape future curricula, and articulate the field’s contributions to broader academic domains amid institutional mergers and shifting disciplinary boundaries in higher education.

items.title: LLM Maintainer: A Judge-in-the-Loop Framework for Continuous Quality Monitoring and Regression Detection in Deployed Large Language Model Systems
items.abstract: Large language model (LLM) systems deployed in production are subject to a form of degradation that classical software is not: their behavior can change without a corresponding code change, because the underlying model, its provider-side weights, or the prompt scaffolding around it can shift independently of the application's own release cycle. Traditional regression testing, built around deterministic assertions, is poorly suited to this setting, because LLM outputs are open-ended, stochastic, and evaluated along dimensions –– tone, faithfulness, safety, format compliance –– that resist exact-match comparison. This paper presents LLM Maintainer, an open-source tool that treats a second LLM call as a judge, scoring a fixed suite of "golden prompts" against natural-language rubrics on every run, persisting the results, and flagging statistically meaningful drops relative to a rolling per-test-case baseline. We describe the system's architecture –– a YAML-configured test suite, an execution runner, a structured LLM-as-judge module, a regression-detection algorithm, a SQLite persistence layer, and a Flask dashboard –– and its command-line and dashboard-triggered workflows for both ad hoc and scheduled (cron-style) use. Because this work was produced in a network-restricted sandbox without access to the live Anthropic API, we report a fully disclosed, seeded, synthetic case study rather than presenting simulated data as genuine field results: we ran the actual, unmodified runner, judge, regression-detection, and persistence code for 30 simulated daily evaluation cycles (180 evaluated prompt-response pairs) against a six-case suite modeling a retail-banking customer-support assistant, with three deliberately injected incidents –– a transient API failure, a silent quality regression introduced by a system-prompt refactor, and a one-off output-format violation. The tool's naive, fixed-threshold rolling-baseline detector recovered five of six injected anomalies (83.3% recall) but also raised 18 flags attributable to ordinary sampling variance in a five-point ordinal judge scale (21.7% precision, F1 = 0.345), a quantitative finding that motivates statistically smoothed alternatives. We situate this design relative to LLM-as-a-judge evaluation research, holistic benchmarking, documented behavioral drift in commercial LLMs, and concept-drift detection in classical machine learning operations, and we discuss the threats to validity inherent in judge-based scoring –– including self-preference and verbosity bias –– alongside concrete mitigations. We conclude that continuous, judge-in-the-loop regression testing is a necessary complement to pre-deployment benchmarking for maintaining LLM-integrated software, while cautioning that naive thresholding requires the same statistical care long established in the concept-drift literature.

items.title: LLM4FL: Multi-Agent Fault Localization via Graph Navigation and Verbal Reasoning
items.abstract: Locating and fixing software faults is challenging. Traditional Spectrum-Based Fault Localization (SBFL) uses test coverage and failure data but often suffers from low accuracy due to a lack of semantic understanding of code. Deep-learning approaches can improve localization, but require extensive training data and computational resources. Recent Large Language Models (LLMs) offer a promising alternative with stronger code reasoning capabilities. However, existing LLM-based fault localization techniques still struggle at the repository level due to large context windows and positional bias, in which important debugging signals may be buried in large contexts. In this work, we introduce LLM4FL , a multi-LLM-agent-based fault localization technique designed to address these challenges. LLM4FL uses three specialized agents. The Context Extraction Agent divides and prioritizes covered methods into token-fitting groups using an order-aware strategy based on Ochiai suspiciousness scores. The Debugger Agent navigates the repository through graph-based retrieval to generate failure reasoning and rank suspicious methods. The Reviewer Agent then re-evaluates and re-ranks the results through iterative self-refinement and verbal reasoning. Evaluated on Defects4J, LLM4FL improves Top-1 accuracy over prior LLM-based approaches, including AutoFL and SoapFL , by 14.5% and 4.58%, respectively. Our ablation study further highlights the importance of LLM4FL's design choices, with failure reason generation improving Top-1 performance by 12.5% and order-aware division substantially improving localization accuracy by 18.07%.

items.title: Machine Learning and Deep Learning in Modern Healthcare: Clinical Applications, Public Health Implications, Cybersecurity Threats, and Ethical Considerations
items.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI), Machine Learning (ML) and Deep Learning (DL) are transforming the way modern medicine is practiced, with more accurate disease detection, clinical decision making, personalized medicine, and public health surveillance. This paper reviews their applications in clinical medicine, epidemiological surveillance, digital health technologies and population health care. It also includes cyber security threats like privacy issues, enemy attacks, and data breaches, ransom ware. Ethical, legal and technical aspects such as algorithmic bias, data confidentiality, transparency and compliance with regulations are also discussed. New technologies like Generative AI, federated learning, and Explainable AI provide ways to build secure, efficient, and trustworthy healthcare systems.

items.title: Making the Model Visible: Modelling Performance and Methodological Provenance in an AI-Assisted Digital Humanities Workflow
items.abstract: The South African College of Music (SACM) at the University of Cape Town holds a substantial collection of concert recordings and accompanying programme data. Preparing this material for publication through Ibali: Digital Collections UCT required relationships implicit in the original spreadsheets to be represented explicitly within Omeka S. This paper examines the development of a linked-resource model structured around four resource types: Concert, Performance, Work and Performance Credit. Particular attention is given to distinguishing a musical Work from an individual Performance, and to representing performer participation as a separate resource when information such as instrument, voice type or character belongs to the relationship itself. The paper also considers practical consequences of the model, including the use of stable identifiers across successive imports and the challenge of creating meaningful labels for relational resources within the user interface. The model was developed iteratively with generative AI used to explore structures, generate data-transformation methods and test possible representations. Drawing on this process, the paper argues that data modelling makes interpretive distinctions computationally visible, while significant human-AI modelling decisions should themselves form part of the methodological provenance through which digital humanities resources can later be understood and reused.

items.title: Markerless three-dimensional biomechanical analysis of manual flexible ureteroscopy: experience-related differences in wrist load during lower-calyx access
items.abstract: Purpose To quantify upper-limb kinematics and estimated biomechanical load (a kinematics-derived load proxy, not measured muscle force) during simulated manual flexible ureteroscopy (fURS) using markerless 3D pose estimation, testing whether experience-related differences concentrate in lower-calyx access. Methods Eighteen urologists (10 experts, 8 novices) performed a phantom task: renal pelvis to upper, middle and lower calyx, returning to the pelvis between calyces. 3D landmarks from smartphone video (MediaPipe Pose) were converted to joint angles, jerk and inverse-dynamics load estimates. Primary outcomes were right-wrist force, jerk and angle in the lower-calyx phase; others were exploratory, analysed with participant-level Welch tests, Hedges g, 95% CIs, Holm correction and a mixed model for group × phase interaction. Results Procedure time was longer in novices (115.5 vs 61.5 s). In the lower-calyx phase, novices showed higher right-wrist force (1.87 vs 1.16 N; Holm p = 0.026), jerk (Holm p = 0.020) and angle (31.6° vs 24.9°; Holm p = 0.026), with no upper-calyx differences; force and jerk showed significant group × phase interactions (p = 0.004, 0.007) but angle did not (p = 0.35). Force, jerk and dispersion correlated strongly with movement speed (ρ = 0.93–0.99), and group differences were attenuated after speed adjustment. Conclusion In this simulator study, experience-related differences in estimated wrist load emerged mainly during lower-calyx access, whereas wrist angle differed throughout, pinpointing an ergonomic target. Because estimates were kinematics-derived and not EMG-validated, findings are hypothesis-generating; correlating them with physiological muscle activity is an important next step for robot-assisted ureteroscopy design.

items.title: Mathematics Anxiety and Level of Motivation as Predictors of the Academic Achievement of Public Senior High School Students
items.abstract: Identifying students at risk of low mathematics achievement before grades are released requires markers that can be measured early. This study examined mathematics anxiety and level of motivation as predictors of the academic achievement of 109 Grade 11 and 12 students of General Santos City National High School in School Year 2025–2026. A descriptive-correlational design was used. Anxiety was measured in emotional, physiological, cognitive, and behavioral dimensions and motivation in intrinsic, extrinsic, and amotivation dimensions, using instruments adapted from the Abbreviated Math Anxiety Scale and the Academic Motivation Scale that showed acceptable to good reliability (α = .78 to .85). Achievement was measured through first- and second-quarter mathematics grades. Students were both highly anxious and highly motivated: extrinsic motivation ranked highest (M = 3.30, Very High), followed by intrinsic motivation, emotional anxiety, and cognitive anxiety (M = 3.23 each, High), while amotivation was Fair (M = 2.28). Achievement was Satisfactory, with mean grades rising from 83.45 to 84.20. Age, sex, grade level, strand, and family income were associated with both predictors, and sex, grade level, and strand with achievement. Mathematics anxiety was a moderate negative correlate of achievement (r = −.42, p = .001; 17.6% shared variance), and motivation a moderate positive correlate (r = .38, p = .002; 14.4%). Both variables are useful indicators of achievement risk and resilience, although their unique predictive contributions require regression-based confirmation. A mental health plan built on early screening and tiered support is proposed.

items.title: Mathematics Anxiety and Level of Motivation in Relation to the Academic Performance of Public Senior High School Students
items.abstract: Many Filipino senior high school students fear mathematics, and this fear may undermine their performance in a subject that shapes their college and career options. This study examined mathematics anxiety and motivation levels among public senior high school students in relation to their academic performance. Using a descriptive-correlational design, it surveyed 109 Grade 11 and 12 students of General Santos City National High School, selected through stratified random sampling, in School Year 2025–2026. A 20-item anxiety questionnaire adapted from the Abbreviated Math Anxiety Scale and a 15-item motivation questionnaire adapted from the Academic Motivation Scale were pilot-tested (α = .78 to .85), and first- and second-quarter mathematics grades were taken from school records. Results showed High anxiety in all four dimensions, led by emotional and cognitive anxiety (M = 3.23 each). Nervousness when solving problems in front of the class (3.40), a faster heartbeat before examinations (3.35), and difficulty recalling formulas during tests (3.30) were Very High. Extrinsic motivation was Very High (M = 3.30), driven mainly by grades and careers, while intrinsic motivation was High (M = 3.23) and amotivation was Fair (M = 2.28). Performance was Satisfactory, with mean grades rising from 83.45 to 84.20. Anxiety and motivation were significantly related to age, sex, grade level, strand, and family income, and performance to sex, grade level, and strand. Anxiety correlated moderately and negatively with performance (r = −.42, p = .001), and motivation correlated moderately and positively (r = .38, p = .002). Anxiety concentrated in evaluative situations, and external motivation appears to have sustained students’ effort. A mental health plan addressing stress, confidence, relevance, and family support is proposed.

items.title: Mathematics Anxiety and Level of Motivation: Effects to the Academic Achievement of Public Senior High School Students
items.abstract: Mathematics anxiety remains a persistent barrier to achievement among Filipino senior high school students, yet its interplay with motivation has received limited local attention. This study examined the effects of mathematics anxiety and motivation level on the academic achievement of 109 Grade 11 and 12 students at General Santos City National High School during School Year 2025–2026. Using a descriptive-correlational design, the study measured anxiety in emotional, physiological, cognitive, and behavioral dimensions and motivation in intrinsic, extrinsic, and amotivation dimensions through pilot-tested instruments (Cronbach’s α = .78 to .85), and obtained first- and second-quarter mathematics grades from school records. Data were analyzed using frequencies, percentages, weighted means, chi-square, and Pearson correlations. Students reported a high level of mathematics anxiety, most intense in emotional and cognitive forms (M = 3.23 each), with nervousness during public problem-solving (3.40) and difficulty recalling formulas during exams (3.30) rated Very High. Extrinsic motivation was Very High (M = 3.30), intrinsic motivation was High (M = 3.23), and amotivation was Fair (M = 2.28). Mathematics achievement was Satisfactory and improved from a mean of 83.45 to 84.20 across quarters. Age, sex, grade level, strand, and family income were significantly related to both anxiety and motivation, while sex, grade level, and strand were related to achievement. Mathematics anxiety was moderately and negatively correlated with achievement (r = −.42, p = .001), and motivation was moderately and positively correlated with it (r = .38, p = .002). The findings indicate that anxiety depresses and motivation sustains mathematics performance. A comprehensive mental health plan integrating stress management, confidence-building instruction, relevance-based teaching, family engagement, and teacher capacity building is recommended.

items.title: Measuring and Enhancing Digital-Intelligence Literacy: An Empirical Study in Zhejiang, China
items.abstract: The rapid advancement of generative artificial intelligence (GAI) is accelerating the transformation of digital society from “tool-based application” to “intelligent collaboration,” creating demand for composite competencies in technical operation, ethical awareness, and human–AI collaboration. To address limitations in existing digital literacy frameworks, particularly their inadequate treatment of cognitive overload, ethical risks, and disparities in the depth of GAI use, this study proposes the concept of “digital-intelligence literacy” (DIL) and constructs a comprehensive five-dimensional evaluation framework comprising Data-Inquisitive, Synergistic-Adaptive, Digital-Content-Hermeneutic, Ethico-Security, and Solution-Application literacies. Using 667 stratified random survey samples from Zhejiang Province, China, and employing principal component analysis, one-way ANOVA, structural equation modeling (SEM), and LASSO regression, this study systematically examines the current status, group disparities, and underlying mechanisms of DIL. The findings reveal the following: significant disparities in DIL across age groups, education levels, and GAI usage frequency, with older adults and low-frequency users encountering prominent challenges; GAI cognition emerges as the most critical factor for improving DIL, substantially exceeding the influence of attitudes and environmental perceptions; a core competency transformation chain of “Synergistic-Adaptive → Digital-Content-Hermeneutic → Solution-Application” literacy revealed by SEM, alongside dynamic interaction between safety-ethics and technological exploration; and participation intentions in DIL-related education are primarily driven by existing literacy levels, usage habits, and attitudes rather than cognitive factors alone. Based on these findings, this study proposes a “cognition-first, systemic-empowerment” strategy, including nationwide educational initiatives centered on GAI-based general knowledge and differentiated empowerment strategies for key groups, providing empirical evidence for local governments to formulate precise and inclusive literacy enhancement policies.

items.title: Medical Reasoning in Large Language Models: Development and Evaluation of the MedEvalArena Benchmark
items.abstract: Background Large language models (LLMs) perform strongly on medical specialty board multiple-choice questions (MCQs) but underperform in complex medical reasoning. This gap indicates a need to improve LLM medical reasoning and evaluation paradigms. Objective This study aimed to develop and evaluate MedEvalArena, a dynamically regenerable benchmark for assessing medical reasoning in LLMs. Methods In a symmetric round-robin format, 6 frontier LLMs from the OpenAI, Grok, Gemini, Claude, Kimi, and DeepSeek families generated challenging board-style medical MCQs, adjudicated question validity on an ensemble LLM-as-judge panel, and answered the validated examination. Candidate items were generated until each model contributed 50 validated questions according to Association of American Medical Colleges (AAMC)/American Board of Medical Specialties (ABMS) physician specialty distributions, yielding a 300-question examination. Judges adjudicated candidate questions’ logical validity and medical accuracy. We compared question-generation validity rates, assessed leave-one-out judge agreement, and tested for self-judging preference. Questions were audited for overlap with public MedQA (medical question-answering) benchmarks. We tested question-answering (QA) accuracy across LLMs using a binomial-logit generalized linear mixed model likelihood-ratio test. A generator-stratified 90-question subset was completed by 5 board-certified physicians for paired human-LLM analysis. We evaluated inference cost-accuracy tradeoffs. Multiple comparisons were adjusted by the Benjamini-Hochberg (BH) procedure. Results Judge-panel validity rates were significantly higher for questions generated by OpenAI (94.8%, Wilson 95% CI 85.9%-98.2%), Gemini (92.3%, 95% CI 83.2%-96.7%), and Claude (83.3%, 95% CI 72.6%-90.4%) models than those generated by Kimi (63.8%, 95% CI 54.3%-72.4%), Grok (56%, 95% CI 45.8%-65.8%), and DeepSeek (46.0%, 95% CI 37.4%-54.7%). Kimi also demonstrated significantly higher validity than DeepSeek (2-sample tests of proportions; BH-adjusted P =.01). The public-source similarity audit found no exact or near-duplicate matches. Leave-one-out judge agreement was moderate. Generator-specific same-family judging coefficients were nonnegative (0 to 11.0 percentage points); however, none remained significant after BH adjustment. There was no significant difference between the 6 frontier LLM QA accuracies, which ranged from 85.7% (257/300) to 91.7% (275/300), on the 300-question examination (generalized linear mixed model likelihood-ratio test P =.07). The study had 80% power to detect LLM accuracy differences of 9.2 percentage points; nonsignificance did not establish equivalence. On the 90-question subset, physician accuracy was 85.6% (95% CI 79.4%‐91.7%; stratified normal with finite-population correction), compared with aggregate LLM performance of 94.4% (85/90; Wilson 95% CI 87.6%‐97.6%). This difference was not significant (McNemar test, P =.08); however, the study was powered to detect a human vs LLM accuracy difference of 14% to 15%. Answering-only costs varied by nearly 2 orders of magnitude, with multiple models on the cost-accuracy Pareto frontier. Conclusions MedEvalArena enables scalable, regenerable, peer-judged benchmarking of LLM medical reasoning. Question-generation validity differentiated model families more clearly than answering accuracy, suggesting that valid MCQ generation may complement QA benchmarks for assessing LLM medical reasoning.

items.title: Meslek Yüksekokulu Öğrencilerinin Üretken Yapay Zekâya Yönelik Tutumları: Silifke Meslek Yüksekokulu Örneğinde Betimsel Bir Ön Çalışma
items.abstract: Yapay zekâ (YZ) teknolojilerindeki hızlı ivme, yükseköğretimde bilginin üretim, erişim ve aktarım süreçlerini köklü biçimde dönüştürmektedir. Bu dönüşüm, iş gücü piyasasına doğrudan uygulama odaklı ara eleman yetiştiren meslek yüksekokulları (MYO) için stratejik bir öneme sahiptir. Yetkinlik ve uygulama temelli yapıları nedeniyle MYO’larda yapay zekâ entegrasyonunun kendine özgü dinamiklerle ele alınması, bunun için de öncelikle öğrencilerin mevcut durumunun ortaya konulması gerekmektedir. Bu bildiri, Mersin Üniversitesi Silifke Meslek Yüksekokulunda yapay zekâ destekli pedagojik dönüşüm ihtiyaçlarını belirlemeyi amaçlayan yakınsayan karma yöntemli bir yüksek lisans tez çalışmasının ön çalışması niteliğindedir ve yalnızca nicel boyutun betimsel bulgularıyla sınırlıdır. Ön çalışmanın amacı, Silifke MYO öğrencilerinin Üretken Yapay Zekâ (Ü-YZ) teknolojilerine yönelik tutum düzeylerini betimlemektir. Araştırma betimsel tarama modelinde tasarlanmıştır. Çalışma grubunu 2026–2027 eğitim-öğretim yılında Silifke Meslek Yüksekokulunda aktif olarak öğrenim gören öğrenciler oluşturmakta olup evrenin tamamına ulaşılması hedeflenmiştir (tam sayım). Veriler; kullanışlılık, beklenti, yetkinlik ve endişe boyutlarından oluşan 23 maddelik Üretken Yapay Zekâya Yönelik Tutum Ölçeği (SAGAI) ve kişisel bilgi formu aracılığıyla toplanacaktır. Verilerin analizinde betimsel istatistiklerden (frekans, yüzde, aritmetik ortalama ve standart sapma) yararlanılacak; tutum düzeyleri ölçeğin geneli ve alt boyutları düzeyinde, ayrıca cinsiyet, program türü (teknik ve sosyal programlar) ve Ü-YZ kullanım sıklığına göre betimsel olarak raporlanacaktır. Bu ön çalışmada gruplar arası farklara ilişkin çıkarımsal testlere yer verilmeyecektir. Tutumların söz konusu değişkenlere göre farklılaşıp farklılaşmadığının sınanması, öğrenci görüşmelerine dayalı nitel bulgular ve nicel ile nitel bulguların bütünleştirilmesi asıl çalışmanın kapsamında olup ayrıca raporlanacaktır. Elde edilecek betimsel bulguların, MYO öğrencilerinin Ü-YZ’ye yönelik tutumlarına ilişkin genel bir görünüm sunması ve asıl çalışmanın nitel aşamasında derinleştirilecek konuların belirlenmesine temel oluşturması beklenmektedir.

items.title: Misconceptions of artificial intelligence: the modern seer as a synthesis of human knowledge without consciousness, emotion, or moral sill
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence is often depicted in public discourse as either a compliant statistical instrument or an emerging entity endowed with knowledge, creativity, feelings, and intentions that may soon rival human capabilities. Both portrayals are fundamentally flawed, as they rely solely on observable performance and infer internal experiences from social appearances. This Viewpoint advocates for a more rigorous model: conceptualizing artificial intelligence as a modern seer, an intricate system that compresses, retrieves, and recombines recorded human knowledge at scales unattainable by any individual. The Viewpoint develops the seer from a metaphor into an analytical framework. The seer is a consulted but uncertified epistemic authority: its capabilities generate interaction cues, the cues invite inferences of understanding, emotion, intention, and authority, and governance must act on these cues and on the calibration of trust rather than on claims about a machine mind. This model clarifies both the practical utility of these systems and the misguided authority often attributed to them. It demonstrates that synthesis can generate novel insights without consciousness, that affective language can provide reassurance without genuine concern, and that value-sensitive recommendations can be produced without moral agency. These distinctions do not render the technology inherently safe, as systems lacking experience can still amplify errors, entrench biases, concentrate power, and undertake consequential actions. The field of drug development exemplifies these limitations: a model may integrate evidence throughout the pharmaceutical process; nevertheless, biological validation and accountable judgment remain essential. This discussion is no longer solely philosophical; regulatory bodies such as the United States Food and Drug Administration, the European Medicines Agency, the International Committee of Medical Journal Editors, and prominent scientific publishers have each adopted frameworks to evaluate context, risk, credibility, and transparency, none of which directly address machine consciousness. Institutions have already moved beyond metaphor-based policymaking. This Viewpoint encourages scientists and scholars to do the same. It identifies ten misconceptions, eight category errors and two factual errors, traces each to the interaction cue that produces it, and states what the framework adds to existing debates on anthropomorphism, stochastic parrots, responsibility gaps, and context-based governance. Addressing these misconceptions will change how AI systems are tested, trusted, and governed.

items.title: Misinformation and organizational capacity in extension and advisory services: building resilience in the age of artificial intelligence
items.abstract: Extension and Advisory Services (EAS) play a critical role in connecting research, policy, and practice to support millions of farmers worldwide. However, the increasing complexity of information systems and the emergence of powerful digital technologies such as Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Large Language Models (LLMs) have introduced both opportunities and challenges for these organizations. EAS institutions, already constrained by limited budgets and workforce shortages, are under pressure to integrate digital tools while maintaining trust, accuracy, and inclusivity in information dissemination. Historically, EAS organizations have adapted to successive waves of technological change, from the introduction of mobile phones and ICT-based platforms to the widespread use of social media for agricultural communication. Each transformation has required not only technical adaptation but also organizational learning, communication restructuring, and capacity development—both within EAS and among their primary clients, the farmers. The integration of AI technologies presents a new and more complex frontier. While AI can enhance decision support, automate communication, and strengthen data management, it also amplifies risks related to misinformation, data bias, ethical use, and erosion of human-centric extension principles. This perspective paper proposes to examine how misinformation management intersects with the organizational capacity and resilience of EAS systems in the context of rapid technological change. It will explore how EAS organizations can build institutional readiness to detect, counter, and manage misinformation while maintaining trust and credibility in high-stakes decision-making environments. The discussion will draw from communication and resilience theories to highlight pathways for strengthening adaptive capacity—integrating human, technological, and organizational dimensions—to ensure accurate information flows within increasingly digital agri-food systems.

items.title: Mobile Location-Based Recommendation Systems and Local Businesses: Evidence from the Restaurant Industry
items.abstract: When looking for a place to eat, how much do recommendations on your smartphone influence your choice? Can they help restaurants tucked away on side streets thrive in an age of algorithmic recommendations? We studied the launch of a location-based recommendation feature on South Korea’s largest search platform, tracking 16,720 restaurants over eight months. We find that visibility matters, but its benefits are uneven. Restaurants tucked away on side streets, far from subway stops, attracted the most additional attention when recommended by the algorithm. Yet this advantage did not translate into greater intentions to visit. Making a restaurant easier to discover did not necessarily overcome the inconvenience of reaching it. Digital information helped bridge this online-to-offline friction. Hard-to-reach restaurants with stronger online reputations and richer information, including customer reviews, photos, and menus, were better able to turn attention into visit intentions. For small businesses, visibility creates opportunities, but credible information helps turn attention into potential customers. For platforms and policymakers, location-based recommendations can bring overlooked businesses into view, but realizing their potential requires making reliable information readily available to consumers.

items.title: Modeling Steering Times of Oblique 3D Paths
items.abstract: Understanding how users perform steering tasks on planar user interfaces (UIs) presented at oblique angles is important for designing effective interfaces in 3D workspaces such as VR, where the viewer’s angle relative to the content can vary. However, existing steering models have mainly assumed frontal viewing and do not fully account for viewpoint-dependent changes in apparent path geometry. We conducted a VR experiment in which users performed raycasting-based steering on circular paths displayed on a UI plane. We varied the oblique angle ϕ from 0° to 60°. We found that movement time generally increased as ϕ increased, and error rate was significantly higher at 60° than in the 0° , 20° , and 40° conditions. To model this effect, we extended the steering law using apparent path length, apparent width, and projected local curvature computed from the user’s viewpoint. A baseline steering model based only on geometric path length and width on the UI plane achieved an adjusted R 2 of 0.9024, whereas a viewpoint-dependent global steering model based on apparent path length and width achieved an adjusted R 2 of 0.9637. A local curvature-integrated steering model further improved the fit, achieving the highest adjusted R 2 of 0.9910 and the lowest AIC among the compared models. In leave-one-condition-out cross-validation, this model showed the best predictive performance among the compared models. These results show that incorporating how the appearance of geometry changes with the viewpoint improves steering-time prediction in our tested VR setup, which provides quantitative design guidance for spatially fixed UIs.

items.title: MOGAI/LIOM Archive Blogs on Tumblr as Intraplatform Community Archives
items.abstract: Many studies have examined the archiving of social media posts in external repositories such as the Internet Archive, with some research focusing on Tumblr specifically (e.g. Ogden 2022). However, little analysis has been devoted to intraplatform archiving by Tumblr users who run self-appointed archive blogs. This study examines Tumblr blogs that present themselves as archives of MOGAI (Marginalized Orientations, Genders, And Intersex) and LIOM (Labels, Identities, Orientations, and Other Minorities) identity labels and pride flags. To understand how these blogs describe themselves as archives and engage in or eschew established core archival practices, we are collecting a sample of their introductory and FAQ posts and analyzing them through inductive open coding and constant comparison. Preliminary data analysis suggests that MOGAI/LIOM archive blogs are characterized by: (1) a defined content scope, (2) limited or absent rules about whose posts will be reblogged, (3) limited or absent rules about interaction from other users (“Do Not Interact” statements), (4) tagging systems that enable people to more easily find relevant labels or flags, and (5) a focus on supporting the MOGAI/LIOM labeling community. These findings imply that intraplatform MOGAI/LIOM archiving on Tumblr tends to align with contemporary archival philosophies and practices while also being fundamentally shaped by the sociotechnical information landscape of Tumblr.

items.title: Monitoring of the dune for dike pilots: evolution after 5 years
items.abstract: At the beginning of 2021, the MDK Coastal Division, Ostend and Middelkerke municipality built-up dunes on the dry beach in front of a sea dike at four locations: Spinoladijk (Ostend), Raversijde, Westende and Knokke. Intensive monitoring at these Nature-based-Solution (NbS) sites was carried out from the beginning of 2021 (except in Knokke from 12/2023) to 03/2026 to investigate the morphological development and evolution of the built dunes. This report documents evolution of the morphology of the dune for dike pilots until the 5th year after construction. A progressive evolution of the four pilot sites occurred over the entire monitoring period.A substantial accretion took typically place in the 1st year in the zones where marram grass and/or brushwood fences were installed. These allowed to capture effectively the aeolian sand transport. Over time, there has been a reduction in sand trapping which could be related to the saturation of the vegetated boxes as well as a difference of wind condition over the monitoring periods. At Raversijde, this reduction could be further caused by a diminution of sand availability after the nourishment in 2021. A combination of natural and human factors might have caused this in Spinoladijk and Westende. Further monitoring surveys would help to understand the observed relationship between accretion in the upper-part of the dry beach and erosion dominating its lower part. These would also confirm the temporal behaviour and evolution of the NbS sites.

items.title: MOSAIC: Integrating Computer-Vision-Assisted Counting and Multimodal Large Language Models for Species Identification in Mosquito Surveillance
items.abstract: Municipal mosquito control programs depend on timely counts and species identification, yet these tasks take staff time, require scarce expertise, and are often handled in separate tools. We developed MOSAIC (Mosquito Observations and Surveillance using AI for Communities), a web platform bringing trap collections, photographs, counts, laboratory results, and expert review into a single record and turning them into weekly trap priorities. We evaluated it with the vector control program of Corpus Christi, Texas, USA. Counting uses classical computer vision (OpenCV) without a trained model; for identification, we compared multimodal large language models (LLMs) with a laboratory-trained convolutional neural network (CNN) and tested LLMs given a local species list, taxonomic knowledge, and labeled examples. OpenCV counts were within two mosquitoes of the operators’ blind counts for 69% of 175 collections. On citizen-science photographs, the zero-shot LLM was correct on 89% of the genera it named but named a genus for 83% (overall accuracy 74%, versus 77% for the CNN). Across three runs, added knowledge and examples raised mean forced-choice species accuracy from 17 to 20% to 63–70%, but when abstention was allowed, the models named a species for only 23–49% of specimens. Automated tools can assist surveillance while experts confirm the outputs.

items.title: Nanocomposite Formulations for Biologics and Peptide Delivery: Recent Advances, Challenges, and Future Perspectives
items.abstract: Biologics, comprising therapeutic peptides, proteins, enzymes, antibodies, vaccines, and nucleic-acid-based drugs, have created a new dimension in pharmacotherapy by virtue of their molecular mechanism of action, which goes beyond the scope of traditional pharmacological agents. Despite their clinical promise, they are often associated with various physiological and physicochemical barriers that limit their therapeutic efficacy. Peptides and protein drugs are highly susceptible to enzymatic and chemical degradation, as well as hydrolytic cleavage as a result of exposure to the challenging in vivo environment. Additionally, their large size and hydrophilicity contribute to poor permeability across biological membranes and rapid clearance from circulation after administration. Nanocomposite solution Nanocomposite formulations allow designing nanomaterials in which two or more chemical compounds or units are combined to form an aggregate or a supramolecular structure with characteristic properties that differ from those possessed by each component. Polymer-nanoparticle, lipid-polymer, inorganic-polymer, hydrogel-nanoparticle, nanofibers, and biomimetic structures can be used to create nanocomposite materials for carrying various types of cargo with different physicochemical properties. At the same time, such particles can protect the delivered substance and actively interact with various barriers and cells, tissues, and organisms. Unlike many traditional nanocarriers, nanocomposite particles can have multiple components, allowing their independent control to achieve the desired overall effect. Recent Advances Recent research trends have shifted from conventional encapsulation strategies toward multifunctional designs involving mucus penetrating, receptor-mediated, stimuli-responsive, endosomal escaping, biomimetic, microfluidic, and formulation-optimized approaches. Lipid-polymer hybrid nanoparticles have emerged as promising systems for protein and peptide drug delivery due to the possibility to combine the advantages of polymers and lipids. Mesoporous silica allows for the construction of systems with diverse pore structures and surface chemistry to control the release of macromolecules, while chitosan-based systems have been explored for oral and mucosal peptide delivery. Nanofibers and biomimetic systems offer alternative strategies for transmucosal delivery or engineering of cell interfaces. Challenges Despite an extensive preclinical exploration, the clinical translation of peptide and protein nanocarriers remains limited. Key challenges include biologic stability during processing and storage, formulation uniformity, aggregation, lot-to-lot variability, manufacturability, sterilization, scale-up, physico-biological complexity, immunotoxicity, and insufficient characterization. Regulatory evaluation is inherently product- and quality-driven and requires systematic physicochemical and clinical characterization rather than a binary good/bad assessment of nanoscale features. Future Perspectives The next generation of advanced delivery systems will employ rational material design, microfluidic fabrication, bio-inspired systems, predictive and mechanistic modeling, artificial intelligence/machine learning, and Quality by Design paradigm. Artificial intelligence/machine learning is expected to play an important role in multi-variable formulation design and critical quality attribute prediction, but the complexity of biological systems and the limitations of available data may impede progress. Conclusion: Nanocomposites for Peptide/Protein Delivery Nanocomposite materials offer attractive opportunities for biologic drug delivery due to the possibility to combine multiple functionalities. However, the value of most nanocomposite systems for peptide/protein delivery should be evaluated from the perspective of biologic stability, pharmacokinetics, mechanism of action, safety, and manufacturability. Progress in this area will rely on controlled complexity that is grounded in biologic rationale, amenable to analytical characterization, scalable, and clinically relevant.

items.title: Navigating sustainability tensions at work: Towards sustainable human performance work systems
items.abstract: Purpose This study develops Sustainable Human Performance Work Systems (SHuPWS) to explain how HR systems can address the tensions created by integrating sustainability into strategic human resource management. Design/methodology A systematic review of 108 Scopus-indexed articles identifies recurring tensions, theoretical perspectives, and sustainability-oriented HR practices. The synthesis integrates stakeholder theory, the resource-based view, and the ability–motivation–opportunity framework across macro, meso, and micro levels. Findings Five interdependent tensions concern short- and long-term priorities, organisational performance and employee well-being, dualistic and paradoxical thinking, autonomy and standardisation, and business-oriented and values-based sustainability. SHuPWS are conceptualised as configurations of interdependent HR practices that connect economic, social and environmental objectives with employee well-being, voice, capability development and sustainable effort. Ability-, motivation- and opportunity-enhancing practices are proposed to influence short- and medium-term processes contributing to triple-bottom-line outcomes. These relationships vary across configurations, time horizons, and institutional and organisational conditions. Originality/value The study advances sustainable HRM research by identifying sustainability tensions within the design and operation of HR systems. The framework incorporates configurational, temporal and contextual variation into the explanation of system effects over time. It connects stakeholder expectations, organisational capabilities and employee experience within a multilevel account, and specifies relationships for subsequent empirical examination.

items.title: Negotiating Creative Agency in AI-Assisted Music Production: Insights from Filipino Music Producers
items.abstract: As generative AI becomes integrated into creative practice, understanding how creative agency is negotiated during human–AI collaboration has become a challenge for Human–Computer Interaction (HCI). This paper reports preliminary findings from a qualitative study involving semi-structured interviews with three Filipino music producers who incorporate generative AI into their workflows. Inductive analysis identified negotiation moments through which participants determined where and how generative AI could participate and how AI-generated contributions should be evaluated, modified, and incorporated. We use negotiation moments as an emerging analytical lens for understanding how creators regulate AI participation while exercising creative agency. Rather than treating AI as an autonomous collaborator or passive tool, participants determined the scope of AI involvement and retained human judgment over how AI contributions became part of their work. These preliminary findings offer an HCI perspective on how creative AI systems might support human decision-making and creative control.

items.title: NOESIS CONTINUUM Persistent Experience-Based Learning, Evidence-Guided Revision, and Scoped Verification of Decision Transitions
items.abstract: Systems that act over long periods must do more than generate responses: they need to preserve useful experience, recover context-specific procedures, revise previously accepted knowledge when evidence changes, and constrain consequential state transitions through inspectable checks. We present Noesis Continuum, a single-author systems architecture combining persistent CanonicalMemory with a bounded active working set and dynamically expanding archive; an evidence and dependency graph (GraphOS); bounded alternative generation and applicability exploration (Labyrinth); feedback-based active trials and knowledge admission; scoped transition artifacts (BAPT); finite-horizon continuity checking (BAPT-F); and conditional recovery synthesis using Google OR-Tools CP-SAT. The central contribution is their developmentstage integration into a common learning-and-decision lifecycle rather than a new foundation model or an assertion of universally correct decisions. In author-reported controlled runs, a single A–E learner retained 16/16 declared abilities after four subsequent context admissions (reported maximum observed forgetting 0 on this inventory). With a 4,000byte active budget and non-destructive archive, it retained 16/16 checks, compared with 6/16 for a destructive-eviction negative control with different total physical storage. Relevant source recall succeeded in four development setups with up to 500 distractors. In an authored OR-to-AND ablation, Labyrinth supplied an unavailable AND candidate and GraphOS reduced failed trials from one to zero. In a modeled recovery scenario, CP-SAT constructed an action restoring a declared invariant, followed by BAPT-F POLICY_CERTIFIED over two specified traces; a later integrated recovery used an admitted learner method and retained 16/16 abilities. Task-outcome-driven revision progressed from OR-only v1 to scoped OR/AND v2 and OR/AND/XOR v3, with all three contextual probes at 1.0 and 16/16 original checks retained. These results constitute a substantive controlled systems-integration milestone, not independent proof of general continual learning, broad verification soundness or superiority to strong replay/retrieval baselines. We provide a claim-to-evidence ledger, detailed negative-result register and pre-specified next-stage evaluation requirements. items.abstract: Generative AI (GAI) can support writing, but learners may respond differently to its guidance. This study examined whether field dependence–independence (FDI) moderated the effect of GAI guidance on critical thinking behaviors (CTB) during human–AI collaborative writing. In a mixed-design study, 65 journalism students completed news-writing tasks with Standard GAI, which provided direct responses, and Heuristic GAI, which elicited learners’ reasoning. We coded 696 user prompts as CTB or non-CTB and analyzed them with logistic generalized linear mixed-effects models. Heuristic GAI was associated with more CTB overall, but its effect decreased as GEFT scores increased: students toward the field-dependent end showed larger increases in CTB and greater uptake of cognitive guidance. Source-specific analyses located this heterogeneity primarily in learners’ uptake of cognitive guidance; neither the condition nor moderation effect was significant for learner-initiated CTB. The findings support learner-sensitive GAI scaffolding in educational HCI.

items.title: Nutrient Composition and Profile-Specific Adaptation of ChatGPT-Generated Gluten-Free Diet Plans Compared With Expert Dietitian Reference Plans
items.abstract: We compared 72 ChatGPT-generated gluten-free menus obtained across three sessions with 24 expert-reviewed reference menus for eight simulated adult profiles and three diet patterns. Primary paired analyses used eight profile-level observations per pattern, with Benjamini–Hochberg false-discovery-rate (FDR) adjustment across 90 exploratory tests. Mediterranean ChatGPT menus contained less carbohydrate and more protein and fat as percentages of energy than expert references. Low-carbohydrate ChatGPT menus had higher energy (+243 kcal/day, FDR q=0.025) and lower estimated cost (−52 TRY/day, q=0.035). Leave-one-profile-out analyses retained the direction of these effects. A 96-record audit identified one inconsistent source protein percentage; uniformly recalculated 4–4–9 percentages preserved the direction of principal contrasts but changed the FDR classification of one high-protein contrast. Soluble and insoluble fibre data were insufficiently validated and were excluded from headline conclusions. Retrospective adult-equation energy targets placed 21 of 24 unchanged expert menus within ±10% of target; 18 of 24 fulfilled their study-specific macronutrient ranges. These findings describe differences from an imperfect expert comparator, not clinical nutritional adequacy or gluten-free safety.

items.title: OncoTrack: LLM-based Structured Extraction and Progression Summarization from Longitudinal Oral Cancer Records
items.abstract: Oral cancer poses a significant global health challenge, with patient management heavily reliant on prior case notes and reports. Manual extraction of critical clinical features from unstructured patient records is often time-consuming, labour intensive, expensive, inconsistent, and prone to human error, hindering timely insights into disease progression and effective clinical decision-making. The proposed work, ``OncoTrack'', introduces an AI-powered pipeline to automatically extract relevant clinical data from oral cancer documents and generate progression summaries. The system leverages a fine-tuned Large Language Model (LLM), specifically Meta-Llama-3.1-8B, for extracting 24 clinically relevant tracking features from longitudinal records. In the initial 90:10 experiment on a curated 100-document AIMS cohort, the model achieved approximately \((87.83% \pm 1.81)\) accuracy and \((86.80% \pm 2.00)\) accepted-match precision after \((10)\) epochs of Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) fine-tuning. The evaluation was then extended to a broader, heterogeneous document pool (total processed: 674), where the retained 339-instance held-out analysis produced an overall average normalized field accuracy of \((79.97%)\) and precision of \((73.45%)\) after excluding sparse or inference-heavy fields from the aggregate score; across all 24 fields, average accuracy was \((70.37%)\). The weakest temporal field was `lastFU', which achieved \((0.00)\) accuracy in the initial test set and approximately \((9.44%)\) accuracy in the expanded evaluation. The `lastFU' was not present in most of the documents scanned by the LLM which explains the low accuracy. Subsequent summarization of extracted features is performed by Google's Gemma 3 4b model. The web application and RAG-based assistant are presented as research-prototype components that require independent evaluation, security validation, and clinical workflow assessment before deployment.

items.title: OPPORTUNITIES AND LIMITATIONS OF THE TOOLS IN THE SYNTACTICAL ANALYSIS OF COMPLEX SENTENCES IN ENGLISH AND UZBEK LANGUAGE
items.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has opened new avenues for research in the field of languages, especially in syntactic analysis and comparative studies. Special emphasis is given to the identification of main and subordinate clauses, the detection of syntactic relations and problems that stem from structural differences of the two languages. English is often using conjunctions, relative pronouns, and relatively fixed word order for subordinate relations, while Uzbek is using much agglutinative morphology, subordinate verb forms and constructions for clause-linking. Based on comparative syntactic analysis and a survey of related literature, the paper proposes that the outputs of AI can be critically evaluated by human researchers and thus can be used as a useful tool for linguistic research and grammar teaching. Special focus is placed on the significance of using language accurately, interpreting it contextually, and responsibly utilizing generative AI for multilingual education.

items.title: Optimising Research Abstracts for Scholarly Communication and Discoverability: A Critical Review of Structure, Content and Writing Practices
items.abstract: Scholarly publishing has grown quickly, and researchers now depend on electronic databases to find their way through it. That shift has turned the research abstract into more than a summary. It is often the first part of a paper that a reader, reviewer, editor, or search algorithm sees, and sometimes it is the only part they see. This paper is a critical narrative review of what the literature says about how effective abstracts are structured and written, with particular attention to scholarly communication and digital discoverability. We drew on work covering abstract structure, structured and unstructured formats, reporting completeness, spin, readability, keyword selection and, more recently, the use of generative AI to write abstracts, and we updated the evidence base with studies published between 2020 and 2026. The picture is fairly consistent. A good abstract gives an accurate, concise and self-contained account of the problem, objective, methods, principal findings and conclusion. Structured formats usually help with organisation, searching and peer review, although the benefit varies by discipline and journal. The same weaknesses keep appearing: thin methods and results, too much background, vague wording, conclusions that outrun the data, abstracts that drift from the full paper, and keywords chosen with little strategy. Recent audits show that even in fields with mature reporting guidelines, abstracts typically report well under two-thirds of the recommended items. We bring these strands together in the ABSTRACT Optimisation Framework, which has eight dimensions: Accuracy, Brevity, Structure, Transparency, Results, Accessibility, Clarity and Terminology. The framework is intended as a practical reference for researchers, postgraduate students, supervisors, reviewers and journal editors.

items.title: Pavement crack analysis and detection: A system-oriented survey and unified taxonomy
items.abstract: Pavement crack analysis is a representative benchmark problem for intelligent visual inspection, requiring detection of thin, low-contrast, topologically irregular structures under severe class imbalance. Existing surveys remain fragmented across levels of abstraction, typically addressing algorithmic performance, data acquisition, or management systems in isolation. This survey provides a system-oriented synthesis based on a unified taxonomy with three functional layers: (i) data acquisition and sensing; (ii) crack detection and analysis algorithms, from classical vision to advanced Deep Learning, including foundation models, Large Language Models (LLMs), and Vision-Language Models (VLMs); and (iii) downstream applications, comprising predictive maintenance and Digital Twins. Public datasets and evaluation practices are reviewed, examining how task formulation, annotation granularity, sensing modalities, and acquisition conditions affect evaluation validity and generalization. Computational and deployment considerations (efficiency, interpretability, scalability, and robustness) are then discussed to guide the development of pavement crack analysis solutions that are both scientifically rigorous and practically deployable.

items.title: Penguatan Literasi Membaca Siswa SD melalui Pembelajaran Kreatif Berbasis Cerita Lokal Bernilai Keagamaan di Desa Muktiwari, Cibitung, Bekasi
items.abstract: Reading literacy remains a major challenge in improving the quality of primary education in Indonesia, particularly in rural areas, including Muktiwari Village, Bekasi Regency. Although the village has a Multicultural Village Library and the “Ayo Gemar Membaca” (Let’s Love Reading) program, their use has not been optimal because literacy instruction remains conventional, reading materials based on local wisdom are limited, and religious values have not been systematically integrated into literacy activities. This community service program aimed to strengthen elementary students’ reading literacy through creative multimedia-based learning using local stories with religious values. The program was conducted in May–June 2026 and involved 66 fifth-grade students in Muktiwari Village. It comprised socialization and needs assessment, program preparation, learning implementation, mentoring and evaluation, and sustainability planning. The learning activities included reading motivation, an artificial intelligence (AI)-based animated film entitled Nawawi Sang Penebar Kebaikan, an interactive Stop and Thinking role play, and a literacy treasure hunt. Evaluation was conducted through observation, interviews, and analysis of Group Worksheets (LKK). Most students responded positively, understood the story and its religious values, and all groups completed the worksheets correctly. These results indicate that integrating AI-based multimedia, local stories, active learning, and religious values creates a more engaging, contextual, and meaningful literacy experience. The program also produced modules, learning media, and literacy tools recommended for integration into the School Literacy Movement (GLS) and the “Ayo Gemar Membaca” program to ensure sustainability.

items.title: Perceived AI agreement and teacher support for reasoned dissent in relation to intellectual humility and counterevidence seeking
items.abstract: Introduction When students feel that generative artificial intelligence (AI) agrees with them, do they remain willing to acknowledge possible error and seek evidence against their own views? We distinguished AI support for an answer from teacher support for questioning an answer. We examined how perceived AI agreement and teacher support for reasoned dissent relate to state intellectual humility and reported counterevidence seeking. Methods We surveyed 386 undergraduates, mainly first-year students, at one vocational and technical university. Students completed the questionnaire in class after an AI-assisted English learning task. A separate pilot sample informed the measurement model. Confirmatory factor analysis and structural equation modeling examined the associations, with bootstrap intervals for indirect associations. Results In the main model, perceived AI agreement and teacher support were positively associated with intellectual humility. Humility was positively associated with reported counterevidence seeking. The estimated indirect associations involving humility were positive for both predictors. Their bootstrap intervals excluded zero, with no clear difference between the two estimates. Neither direct path was statistically significant in the main model. Discussion These initial findings suggest that perceived support for one’s view and encouragement to question claims should be considered together when examining humility and counterevidence seeking in AI-assisted learning.

items.title: Perceived Quality of AI-Enabled Social Media Intelligence and Sustainable Brand Perception: A Sequential Mediation Analysis
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has changed how brands communicate with consumers through personalized recommendations, automated responses, and algorithm-driven content on social media. However, favorable evaluations of these interactions may not directly translate into purchasing intentions or positive brand perceptions. This study examines the relationship between perceived AI-enabled social media intelligence quality and sustainable brand perception through the sequential mediating roles of consumer digital trust, electronic word-of-mouth (e-WOM) intention, and purchase intention. Data were collected from 250 Indonesian social media users and analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) with 5,000 bootstrap resamples. The results show that AI-enabled social media intelligence quality is positively associated with digital trust and e-WOM intention. Digital trust is positively associated with e-WOM intention, but its direct relationship with purchase intention is not statistically significant. Both e-WOM intention and purchase intention are positively associated with sustainable brand perception. The hypothesized sequential indirect effect is statistically significant (β = 0.028, p = 0.001). From an information systems perspective, these findings provide empirical evidence linking perceived AI-mediated communication quality to psychological, social, behavioral, and perceptual responses. The study suggests that evaluations of AI-enabled communication systems should consider user trust and recommendation intentions alongside prospective commercial outcomes. Keywords—AI-enabled social media intelligence, digital trust, electronic word-of-mouth, purchase intention, sustainable brand perception, sequential mediation.

items.title: PERSONALIZATION OF DIGITAL ADVERTISING BASED ON DATA AND ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE
items.abstract: Personalization of digital advertising makes it possible to select messages based on user behavior, but greater precision does not always ensure a better response. The research question is under what conditions the specificity of an ad increases its effectiveness. The aim of the paper is to develop a conceptual model for context-sensitive selection of the level of personalization based on a comparison of research findings. The focus is on consumer intent, the timing and placement of the ad, and trust in the way data are used. The paper conducts a thematic comparative analysis of peer-reviewed works that include conceptual models or data from field and laboratory studies of digital advertising. For each source, it compares the factors of personalization, the conditions under which the ad is shown, and the method used to measure the outcome.

The study examines the advantages of adaptive learning platforms, generative language models (LLMs), and automated assessment systems tailored to students' language proficiency levels, learning paces, and individual needs. Furthermore, practical recommendations and methodological approaches for the step-by-step integration of AI tools into the educational framework are presented.

items.title: Plausible Reconstruction Substituted for Captured Detail: Why a Convincing Picture Is Not a Record of What Was There
items.abstract: This conceptual paper introduces Plausible Reconstruction Substituted for Captured Detail, a mechanism by which details supplied from a prior model are mistaken for details recovered from a particular source. A reconstruction may combine recorded information with inferred additions so seamlessly that viewers cannot distinguish what was preserved from what was supplied. Its apparent completeness can then be treated as evidence of fidelity, although natural appearance and faithful recovery are separate properties. The paper assesses reconstruction by distinguishing captured detail from perceptual plausibility. It asks what the surviving record establishes, what additional elements were introduced, which models informed those additions, and whether the inferred portions were identified when the result was displayed or reused. Reconstruction is not inherently misleading or illegitimate. An informed completion may be the best available presentation of incomplete evidence. The mechanism arises when its supplied details acquire the evidential standing of recovered observations. The discussion draws on Frederic Bartlett's account of reconstructive memory and considers research on the relationship between perceptual quality and distortion in image restoration. The first documented case concerns Along the River During the Qingming Festival. A 2018 museum article cited a sign advertising bone-setting as evidence of medical specialization during China's Song dynasty. Subsequent comparison identified the sign in the Qing court version completed in 1736, but not in the earlier scroll attributed to Zhang Zeduan. The second case concerns an ancient Apulian vase acquired by the British Museum in 1867. Two additional heads painted onto a dog's body during nineteenth-century restoration helped scholars identify the scene as Orpheus with Cerberus. Conservation work in 1959 revealed that the original painted dog had one head. The mistaken reconstruction had supplied details on which the interpretation depended. Part of the Representation and Measurement series within On Human Modeling, the paper examines how reconstructed evidence travels, who identifies inferred elements, and how later users can distinguish restoration from observation. Potential applications in human–AI research include image enhancement, generative reconstruction, archival restoration, and evaluation of systems that produce convincing but unverified details from incomplete inputs.

items.title: PREDICTING DISTRIBUTIVE JUSTICE FROM WORK CONTROL AND EMPLOYEE CONTEXT: A MACHINE-LEARNING CLASSIFICATION APPROACH
items.abstract: Understanding the extent to which employees perceive organizational outcomes as fair is crucial in explaining employee attitudes and organizational behaviours. However, while the literature on distributive justice primarily focuses on the outcomes of employees' fairness evaluations regarding pay, rewards, and other organizational outcomes, the extent to which employee control over how the work is performed shapes these evaluations has been relatively less examined. The aim of this research is to examine the predictive relevance of employees' level of control over their work on their perceptions of distributive justice. The research was conducted using data obtained from 246 white-collar and blue-collar employees. In measuring job control, Dwyer and Ganster's (1991) job control approach was utilized, and elements of job control related to task variety, task execution order, work pace, task scheduling, work methods and procedures, and the arrangement of the physical work environment were measured. In the study, a supervised machine-learning classification framework based on nested cross-validation was applied. According to the analysis, among the components of job control, the autonomy to determine the amount of work an individual will do may be informative in distinguishing evaluations of distributive justice. In addition, predicting how decisions will turn out, interacting with people, deciding on the source of information, and job control over wages may help differentiate the evaluations of distributive justice. Organizational tenure has emerged as a potentially relevant contextual predictor carrying predictive information in terms of distributive justice evaluations. The research positions job control as a potential organizational resource linked to distributive justice evaluations; it also offers a methodological contribution to the use of machine learning-based classification in organizational behaviour research. In terms of application, the findings suggest that increasing employees’ control over work processes can contribute to strengthening the perception of justice within organizations.

items.title: Prediction of a task-specific AI-reliance choice from facial expression and galvanic skin response signals
items.abstract: Background Reliance on AI-supported health recommendations is consequential, but a single behavioral source-selection decision is not equivalent to multidimensional psychological trust. Biosignals may contain predictive information before a choice, although small-sample multimodal models require leakage-free evaluation and cautious interpretation. Purpose This study evaluated whether facial-expression probabilities and galvanic skin response (GSR) features predict a task-specific binary choice of an AI-labeled rather than doctor-labeled recommendation in a simulated ADHD assessment. The outcome is treated as a behavioral indicator of reliance rather than a direct measure of psychological trust. Method: This cross-sectional laboratory analysis included a cohort of 60 participants (40 AI-labeled and 20 doctor-labeled choices). Eight facial-expression probabilities and two GSR phasic features were evaluated in prespecified Early (6–3 s) and Proximal (3–0 s) windows. Ten repeats of participant-level stratified five-fold cross-validation were used. Scaling and SMOTETomek resampling occurred only within training folds, and the logistic stacking meta-learner was trained on strictly cross-fitted base-model probabilities. Model-specific 95% confidence intervals and paired AUC differences were estimated with 10,000 stratified participant bootstrap samples; five paired tests were Holm-adjusted. Results Early-window ROC-AUCs were 0.643 (95% CI 0.490–0.786) for Face, 0.430 (0.287–0.578) for GSR, and 0.526 (0.375–0.679) for stacking. Proximal-window ROC-AUCs were 0.550 (0.399–0.699), 0.381 (0.240–0.530), and 0.376 (0.229–0.529), respectively. Stacking did not outperform either modality. Early stacking was worse than Early Face (ΔAUC = −0.116, 95% CI −0.183 to −0.056; Holm-adjusted p = 0.002); the other adjusted paired comparisons were not significant. Conclusion Multimodal stacking did not improve prediction in this small exploratory sample. These results do not establish either a general advantage or a lack of value of multimodal fusion. They do not support deployment or direct trust detection. Larger studies with verified synchronization, repeated decisions, independent trust measures, and external validation are required.

items.title: Predictive models in neurosurgery with machine learning, deep learning, radiomics, and large language models
items.abstract: Background Predictive modeling using artificial intelligence has expanded rapidly across neurosurgical subspecialties, but a focused synthesis of recent evidence is needed to assess performance and methodological quality. Such models may support neurosurgical practice by improving risk stratification, outcome prediction, surgical planning, and individualized decision-making in clinically complex patients Objectives To identify, classify, and critically synthesize predictive modeling studies in neurosurgery published from March 1, 2021, through March 31, 2026, and to evaluate subspecialty distribution, model types, discrimination, external validation, calibration, and methodological quality. Methods A PRISMA 2020-compliant systematic review was conducted using PubMed/MEDLINE and Web of Science. Risk of bias was assessed with PROBAST, and reporting quality was evaluated using TRIPOD. Results Twenty-nine eligible publications were included: 23 primary predictive model studies, 2 large-language-model benchmark studies, and 4 systematic review or quality appraisal studies. Primary studies covered neuro-oncology, cerebrovascular neurosurgery, spine surgery, traumatic brain injury, epilepsy or functional neurosurgery, and pediatric hydrocephalus. Machine learning was the dominant model type. Among the 23 primary predictive-model studies, all reported an extractable discrimination metric, ranging from 0.672 to 0.940, with a median of 0.827 and a mean of 0.818 (SD 0.092). These values represent reported AUC (C-statistic) measures of model discrimination. External validation was reported in 52.2% of primary studies, whereas formal calibration was reported in 26.1% (6/23). Calibration refers to the agreement between predicted probabilities and observed clinical outcomes. Conclusions Predictive AI in neurosurgery shows promising performance across subspecialties, but inadequate calibration reporting and inconsistent external validation remain major barriers to responsible clinical translation. items.title: Preliminary evaluation of a typed decision model for counselling dialogue coding using motivational interviewing
items.abstract: Typed decision models return probabilities over predefined options, potentially supporting automated coding of motivational interviewing transcripts. The study compared Jev 1.13 with ten experts and two large language models (LLMs), Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 sol, on seven motivational interviewing demonstrations. LLMs reported confidence as probabilities. Jev showed high panel agreement, although Claude Opus 5.5 had higher point estimates on both tasks. Against the ten-expert plurality, its estimated calibration error was lower than both LLMs', clearly so only against Claude Opus 5.5. Calibration comparisons depended on the reference; a prespecified target was missed against single coders. Retained successful LLM calls cost 64–175 times as much as Jev’s, with median response times 7–8 times as long. Costs and latencies were measured through one provider on one day. These preliminary findings motivate evaluation in independent clinical sessions and workflows combining automated coding with human review.
